basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 42.' and it opens 'Vers. 42. Tulit annulum de manu sua. Annulus in manu Joseph pontificatum fidei designat,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 42. Tulit annulum de manu sua. Annulus in manu Joseph pontificatum fidei designat, qui in manu, | hoc est in potestate Christi constitutus est. Factus est enim sacerdos secundum ordinem Melchisedech. Stola byssina significat sanctam carnem ejus, quae de terra virgineae carnis exorta est, et sicut byssus diversis passionibus macerata pervenit ad candorem immortalitatis et gloriae sempiternae. Et torquem auream collo circumposuit. Torques aurea, qua collum Joseph ornabatur, sapientiam designat coelestem, quae sicut circulus nec initium habet nec finem. Potest etiam per torquem auream bona voluntas et bonorum simplicitas accipi.
